results.title: Deep Learning for Analyzing Chaotic Dynamics in Biological Time Series: Insights from Frog Heart Signals - ADS
results.content: ## ADS. ## Deep Learning for Analyzing Chaotic Dynamics in Biological Time Series: Insights from Frog Heart Signals. #### Abstract. The study of experimental data is a relevant task in several physical, chemical and biological applications. In particular, the analysis of chaotic dynamics in cardiac systems is crucial as it can be related to some pathological arrhythmias. When working with short and noisy experimental time series, some standard techniques for chaos detection cannot provide reliable results because of such data characteristics. Moreover, when small datasets are available, Deep Learning techniques cannot be applied directly (that is, using part of the data to train the network, and using the trained network to analyze the remaining dataset). To avoid all these limitations, we propose an automatic algorithm that combines Deep Learning and some selection strategies based on a mathematical model of the same nature of the experimental data. To show its performance, we test it with experimental data obtained from ex-vivo frog heart experiments, obtaining highly accurate results. : 10.48550/arXiv.2509.13027.

Title: All signals point to personality: A dual-pipeline LSTM-attention and symbolic dynamics framework for predicting personality traits from Bio-Electrical signals - ScienceDirect
# All signals point to personality: A dual-pipeline LSTM-attention and symbolic dynamics framework for predicting personality traits from Bio-Electrical signals. In this paper, we present a novel methodology for personality trait prediction using a dual-pipeline architecture. The network’s goal is to predict the OCEAN (openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness and neuroticism) traits using physiological signals including: EEG, ECG and GSR. The most universally accepted model for understanding human personality is the Big Five personality model, which includes traits such as extraversion, agreeableness, conscientiousness, emotional stability, and openness [1]. electroencephalogram (EEG), galvanic skin response (GSR) and electrocardiogram (ECG) are among the prominent bio-signals that reflect the complex interplay between an individual’s physiological state and their inherent personality traits. The collected data captures emotional annotations on physiological signals (EEG, ECG and GSR), as well as participants’ Big-five personality traits. By integrating data from these datasets, we aim to capitalize on the efficiency and efficacy of deep learning algorithms for multivariate regression and extend its application to the domain of personality trait prediction [9]. Firstly, the work introduces a novel deep learning network named Attention-based Trait Network (AT3Net) dedicated to personality trait prediction. Such an abstraction layer allows the AT3Net to perceive and recognize patterns at a symbolic level, which is crucial for identifying intricate personality traits embedded within the signals. This provides all-inclusive view of the AT3Net’s predictive capabilities and effectiveness in the context of personality trait prediction. Research in the field of human personality trait prediction using artificial intelligence and machine learning has been progressing rapidly. These methods have been widely employed in various domains, including the prediction of personality traits. Our proposed model Attention-based Trait Network (AT3Net) for predicting the Big Five personality traits using EEG, ECG, and GSR time-series data is shown in Fig. 5. results.title: Deep Learning Dynamics: A Scientific Approach – Data Science and Analytics Thrust
results.content: ## Deep Learning Dynamics: A Scientific Approach. In this talk, I will introduce my a series of works on understanding and improving deep learning via scientific principles and methodology. The success of deep learning depends on both neural networks and optimization dynamcis. I will visit several very foundamental issues in deep learning dynamics: (1) SGD Dynamics and how it selects flat minima; (2) Adam dynamics and how it explains the power of Adam; (3) improving deep learning from a optimization dynamical perspetive; (4) the overlooked pitfalls of weight decay and how to mitigate them; (5) a bridge between protein dynamics and deep learning dynamics. Through this talk, we will also see that scientific principles and theories can provide useful insights and tools for understanding and improving deep learning.
